body:
OK, so that was a fun read. /cc @cdumez @yuki3 as people who I know have been wording on these kind of tricky Web IDL named properties compliance issues.

The section we are looking at is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#past-names-map and afterward. It is indeed very long and complicated. Like @Hixie in https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=22320, I think we are probably all happy to simplify this to anything web-compatible. So let's start with source inspection...
- [Blink](https://codesearch.chromium.org/chromium/src/third_party/WebKit/Source/core/html/HTMLFormElement.cpp?sq=package:chromium&rcl=1473160695&l=753)
- [WebKit](https://github.com/WebKit/webkit/blob/2759f743182b1bb3cc5d4c4d537a8620bf2fdacd/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLFormElement.cpp#L844) (seems identical to nearby Blink code, but I can't find the analog of anonymousNamedGetter)
- Gecko: [todo](http://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/95b0ecf4b59a01e0524ca02f6c96ecaabe38f4d5/dom/html/HTMLFormElement.cpp#1538) + [named getter](http://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/95b0ecf4b59a01e0524ca02f6c96ecaabe38f4d5/dom/html/HTMLFormElement.cpp#1538)

Also, some tests, derived from those in the Bugzilla issue:
- http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4444
- http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4448

Nothing here is great, especially nobody showing the correct values for getOwnPropertyNames. I guess that is reflected in the above code searches by the fact that we're only seeing the named getter, not any ability to actually list the properties. And that's what the original bug was debating about anyway.

In any case, it seems like the goal should just be to come up with some simple algorithm for listing all the properties, in some deterministic order, which "determine the value of a named property" would return something for. I am not really familiar with the constraints here (e.g. is sorting in tree order bad? what else can we sort by?) so do you have any suggestions? Is the past names map ordered?

Basically I am unsure what simplifications we can make without making this less deterministic.

> Nothing here is great, especially nobody showing the correct values for getOwnPropertyNames. 

That is the fundamental problem, yes.

> is sorting in tree order bad?

Somewhat, yes.  Tree-order compares are very much not O(1).  So it's easy to end up in O(N^2) or worse situations once you start tree-order sorting large lists.  Now in practice there's some sorting by tree order happening already on the inputs to whatever our algorithm is, so we may be talking something more like merging multiple sorted lists than doing an overall sort.  It might be possible to do better here than with an overall sort, maybe.

> what else can we sort by?

Therein lies the rub.  You could sort by something like "time of addition to the form", but that means not being able to use a plain hashtable for the internal storage...

> Is the past names map ordered

In Gecko right now it's not; it's just a hashtable.  It's not in the current spec either...  It could be made ordered, probably.

I don't have concrete proposals so far; I would have made them if I did.
/cc @tkent-google as the owner of HTMLFormElement in Blink.
